# Branch office WAN uplinks — FigDown topology

Following the router in the FigDown docs, a `topology` figure declares nodes and the links between them; I kept labels short (ids carry identity, `class` carries the primary/backup meaning) so the figure states structure, not prose.

```figdown
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 topology
title "Branch office WAN uplinks"

class primary "Primary WAN path" stroke=#16a34a
class backup "Backup WAN path (diverse route)" stroke=#dc2626 style=dashed

node access1 "Access Switch 1"
node access2 "Access Switch 2"
node branch "Branch Router"
node hubprimary "Regional Hub A"
node hubbackup "Regional Hub B"

edge access1 branch
edge access2 branch
edge branch hubprimary "primary" class=primary
edge branch hubbackup "backup" class=backup
```

Notes:
- `topology` is dispatchable at `figdown 0.1` but is still EXPERIMENTAL (experimental) — noted here rather than left silent, per the portability guidance.
- The two hub routers are only described as "diverse-path" regional hubs, not further distinguished; I used generic ids `hubprimary`/`hubbackup` as given rather than inventing site names.
- Primary/backup meaning is carried by `class`, not by colour alone, so a reader (or a legend) recovers it from text.

Once built (`node build-svg.js branch-wan-uplinks.fd`), embed as:

```markdown
![Branch office WAN uplinks: two access switches to one branch router, with primary and backup WAN links to two diverse regional hubs](figures/branch-wan-uplinks.svg)

<sub>source: [figures/branch-wan-uplinks.fd](figures/branch-wan-uplinks.fd)</sub>
```
